newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Coal contract boosts Centennial shares.
newsitem.headline: Coal contract boosts Centennial shares.

text.p: Shares in Centennial Coal Co Ltd partly reversed a decline on Thursday after the company said it had been awarded a two-year contract to supply 200,000 tonnes of coal a year to two power stations in New South Wales.
Centennial said the contract from New South Wales generator Delta Electricity was for the supply of the Mt Piper and Wallerawang stations in the state's Lithgow area.
Its Ivanhoe colliery was now fully contracted for the next two years and the company would hold talks with Delta about a longer term agreement.
Centennial shares fell sharply last month after it reported a slump in half-year net profit to December 31 to A$1.1 million from A$2.7 million a year earlier.
Centennial shares were trading up 14 cents at A$1.10 at 3.00 p.m. (0500 GMT), but still well down from about A$1.67 before the release of its half-year results.
